dedupe_keys.name: sinac sistema de informacion nacional de agua de consumo spain

description: SINAC, the National Drinking Water Information System of Spain, is a health information system that records the characteristics of supply systems and the quality of drinking water supplied to the population, run by the Ministry of Health through an internet application. Its aims include detecting and preventing risks from contaminated water, showing local, regional and national water quality and supply features, giving citizens basic information on supply zones and quality, informing authorities and users on infrastructure, coordinating health surveillance programmes, producing periodic reports and meeting reporting duties to the European Union and international bodies. The unit of information is the supply zone, an area no larger than a province where water from one or more sources has homogeneous quality most of the year. There are two kinds of access, professional access for staff of authorities and utilities and public access for citizens. Coverage: national. Access: public information is free, professional access needs an account; the licence is not stated on the page read, and the public query pages were not opened. Caveats: this record is based on the ministry page, and download options for the public are not described. It supports drinking water quality and supply zone analysis and relates to the French SISPEA observatory already in the catalogue.
